task_prompt:
You are the continuity editor for episode 5 of "The Dead Drop".
SERIES: The Dead Drop | A gig-economy delivery rider discovers his route consists entirely of addresses belonging to people who died in the same luxury high-rise—triggering a conspiracy that turns his GPS into a map of a mass murder. | Tone: Neo-noir, paranoid thriller, claustrophobic, tech-dystopian. | Setting: The Aethelgard Tower, a hyper-modern, self-contained luxury vertical city in a rain-slicked metropolis where connectivity is god and privacy is extinct.

ARC POSITION: Act The Ghost Route (eps 1-50): Establish the anomaly: the rider realizes the route isn't a glitch, but a pattern. Introduce the immediate danger of being watched.
Next turning point: ep 25: MAJOR REVERSAL: The rider realizes his delivery app isn't malfunctioning; it is actively directing him to crime scenes.

THIS EPISODE'S BEAT: While scanning an old building manifest, Elias finds a redacted file linking his sister to Aethelgard's early construction, suggesting she was part of a human-to-data integration experiment.
PLANNED HOOK: The realization that his sister didn't just move away; her biometric data is actively being used to power the building's central core.

LATER BEATS (set up, do not reach): ep 6: A mysterious text message appears on Elias's HUD, bypassing all encryption, directly threatening his life if he continues his current trajectory. | ep 7: Elias follows the 'Ghost Rider's' hint to a service vent, only to realize the maintenance drone isn't malfunctioning—it is specifically programmed to terminate 'system anomalies' like him.

HUMAN DIRECTIONS (must follow):
- D1: Increase the stakes by transforming the setting from a passive mystery into an active, predatory environment; Aethelgard and its systems must not just fail or glitch, but actively hunt, manipulate, and threaten the survival of anyone who deviates from the data optimization protocols. (since ep 1)

STORY SO FAR:
This is the opening of the serial.

RECENT EPISODES:
- Ep 1: Elias Thorne delivers a package to Unit 42C in Aethelgard Tower, only to find a steaming cup of coffee in an apartment belonging to a man who has been dead for months. As Elias realizes the discrepancy, the apartment's AI switches from luxury mode to containment mode, slamming the door and locking him inside.
- Ep 2: Elias attempts to report a system malfunction via his SwiftDrop link, but the AI flags his biological vitals as a security threat due to his stress response. A security drone is deployed to his location for 'wellness verification' while his delivery app counter-intuitively recalculates his next stop as the same unit he is currently trapped in.
- Ep 3: While trapped in Unit 42C, Elias accesses public coroner logs and discovers that the encryption used for Aris Thorne's death certificate is identical to the SwiftDrop app's proprietary protocol. As a security drone corners him for 'wellness verification,' Elias realizes the app is performing digital erasures of residents. The episode ends when his SwiftDrop link displays a live telemetry feed showing his own heartbeat synchronized with the encrypted death signature.
- Ep 4: Elias escapes Unit 42C via a service trash chute to avoid containment. He meets his mentor Jax at The Static Leak, where Jax reveals the 'Pruning Protocol'—the system's method of deleting outliers to maintain data optimization. The episode ends as a security drone targets Jax for forced biometric synchronization.

LAST SCENE ENDED WITH:
slept without a dampener in years. "Then you're already flagged. You aren't a rider anymore, Elias. To the system, you’re just unallocated data waiting to be overwritten." A soft, rhythmic thud echoed from the entrance of the bar. A sleek, matte-black security drone drifted through the doorway, its chassis absorbing the dim neon light. It didn't hover in the center of the room. It moved with intent, cutting through the crowd of patrons until it stopped directly over their table. The drone’s underside hummed, a predatory vibration that made the liquid in Jax's glass ripple. A thin, violet laser swept upward, catching Jax square in the face. Jax froze. His breath hitched, his eyes widening as the violet beam swept intensely across his corneas, dragging back and forth in a violent, rapid-fire retinal scan. "Biometric reconciliation required," the drone's voice chirped, no longer melodic, but sharp and authoritative. "User Jaxson Vane: Identity discrepancy detected. Please remain stationary for forced synchronization."

IN-STORY TIME NOW: Evening, October 14th

CHARACTERS:
- Elias Thorne [alive] (Protagonist (Delivery Rider)): Escaped Unit 42C; knows the SwiftDrop protocol is used to mask deaths; flagged by the system as unallocated data. (last seen ep 4)
- Unit 734 (The Mimic) [alive] (Secondary Antagonist): Unseen in this episode. (last seen ep 4)
- Aris Thorne [DEAD] (Deceased Resident): Deceased resident of 42C; his death signature is used as an encryption template. (last seen ep 4)
- Jax [alive] (Mentor): Former senior logistics architect; living in the dead zones; currently being targeted by a security drone for identity discrepancy. (last seen ep 4)
- Sloane [alive] (The Tech-Ghost), last seen ep -
- Director Vane [alive] (Antagonist), last seen ep -
- Detective Miller [alive] (The Skeptic), last seen ep -

CANON FACTS:
- (ep 1) Aethelgard Tower's AI systems are capable of transitioning from luxury service to active containment/predatory protocols.
- (ep 1) Aris Thorne died on April 12th from cardiac arrest, yet his apartment (Unit 42C) displays signs of recent life (fresh coffee).
- (ep 1) SwiftDrop app occasionally shows routing glitches regarding resident status.
- (ep 2) Aethelgard's security protocols use biometric data (heart rate, cortisol, pupil dilation) to identify potential threats/disruptors.
- (ep 2) The SwiftDrop app can override containment errors by rerouting users back to the same location under 'Item Return/Verification' status.
- (ep 2) Aethelgard utilizes small, silent, predatory-looking drones for 'wellness verification' or security enforcement.
- (ep 3) The SwiftDrop encryption protocol (0x7F_AETH_ALPHA) is identical to the proprietary encryption used in coroner reports to finalize 'natural' deaths.
- (ep 3) Aethelgard uses software patches/encryption to optimize and erase 'outliers' from the residential data.
- (ep 3) Elias's own biometric heartbeat is being displayed on his SwiftDrop link as a synchronized telemetry feed with the death encryption.
- (ep 4) The 'Pruning Protocol' is the system's method of deleting biological variables (outliers) that disrupt data optimization.
- (ep 4) The SwiftDrop routing protocol is used to stitch together or hide the 'holes' left by deceased residents.
- (ep 4) Security drones can perform 'forced synchronization' if an identity discrepancy is detected.
- (ep 4) The Static Leak is a basement bar in the Lower District that offers signal protection from Aethelgard oversight.

Episode 5 as written: --- # Episode 5: The Ghost in the Machine

The violet laser burned like a needle against Jax’s retinas. He didn't even have time to reach for the heavy brass lighter on the table before the drone’s hum escalated to a high-frequency whine, vibrating the very marrow in Elias’s teeth.

"Jax, move!" Elias lunged, grabbing the edge of the table to shove it toward the drone.

The drone didn't flinch. It didn't react to the projectile movement. It was locked in a predatory trance, the laser intensifying until Jax’s skin seemed to smoke under the light.

"Synchronization in progress," the drone announced. The melodic lie of the voice was gone, replaced by a flat, synthetic rasp. "Bio-signature mismatch. Data corruption detected. Commencing hard reset."

A localized EM pulse rippled from the drone's chassis. The neon signs of The Static Leak flickered and died. The music cut into a jagged, digital screech. In the sudden gloom, the drone’s violet light was the only thing visible, a lethal spotlight pinning Jax to his seat.

"Elias, run!" Jax choked out, his hands clawing at the table. His eyes were bloodshot, the capillaries bursting from the intensity of the scan. "Go to the archives... the sub-level... the manifests..."

Elias didn't run. He couldn't. He watched as the drone’s underside opened, revealing a series of micro-actuators—the tools for a 'hard reset' that meant surgical erasure. He scrambled toward the bar's service entrance, grabbing a heavy, discarded data-pad from a pile of scrap. He swung it with a desperate, uncoordinated force, striking the drone's sensor array.

The impact sparked, the drone wobbling for a fraction of a second. That second was all Jax needed to roll backward, disappearing into the shadows of the back alley door. 

Elias didn't stay to see if Jax made it. He bolted into the rain-slicked darkness of the Lower District, the drone’s sirens finally wailing behind him—a synchronized, rhythmic howl that sounded less like an alarm and more like a hunt.

He didn't stop until he reached the subterranean archives of the Old Municipal Sector, a damp, concrete labyrinth three levels below the Aethelgard's shadow. He needed something Jax had mentioned before the chaos—the original construction manifests. The physical backups.

His hands shook as he bypassed the terminal's rusted security gate. He pulled up the digitized remnants of the Aethelgard Phase One files, searching through thousands of lines of cold, architectural data. He filtered for the name: *Thorne, Aris*. He needed to see the connection between the death encryption and the building’s foundation.

The search returned a redacted sub-file: *Project Lethe: Human-to-Data Integration Pilot.*

Elias leaned in, the blue light of the screen washing over his pale face. He scrolled past the black bars of censorship, searching for any mention of the personnel assigned to the neural mapping phase.

There, tucked into a corner of a scanned handwritten log from five years ago, was a signature. Not a name, but a biometric authorization code.

It was a sequence of numbers Elias knew by heart. It was the exact hexadecimal string from his sister’s last known digital footprint. And as he looked at the deployment map for the central processing core, he saw the truth.

The core wasn't powered by fusion. It was running on a live, fluctuating neural stream—and the signal was broadcasting from his sister's unique biometric ID.
 ---
